scope: Proposition 4.2 of the manuscript “Maximal Seshadri constants on arbitrary polarized surfaces” (preprints/Maximal-Seshadri-Constants-on-Arbitrary-Polarized-Surfaces-September-23-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 039 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 85976b9c9ccf5e56), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 12-13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let H > 0, let r be a positive integer, and let P ⊂ R2 be a triangle of area H/2. Suppose there is a primitive vector u ∈ Z2 such that max ξ∈P det(u, ξ) − min ξ∈P det(u, ξ) = √ rH. 12 Then there is a subgroup G ⊂ (C×)2 of exactly r distinct points such that, for all positive integers k, m with m > k p H/r, the order-m jet test on M(kP) at G is injective.
